Appendices

Appendix C — The Master Cue Library

A practical reference of 200+ cues grouped by intent for setup, precision, intensity, expression, transition, and recovery.

Use this library as modular language material. Select cues by class phase, participant profile, and objective.

How to use this appendix

  • Choose three to five anchor cues for each phase of your class.
  • Keep cues short during high exertion and more descriptive during preparation or integration.
  • Tag your preferred cues by phase using Module 8 and Module 9.
  • Revise wording when cues create confusion, shame, or avoidable risk.

Setup cues

  1. Plant your feet hip width and feel three points of contact.
  2. Soften your knees enough to stay spring loaded.
  3. Stack ribs over pelvis before the first repetition.
  4. Set your gaze at horizon level to steady orientation.
  5. Spread your toes and grip the floor lightly.
  6. Take one preparatory breath before intensity rises.
  7. Widen your collarbones without flaring your ribs.
  8. Root through heel and big toe together.
  9. Set shoulders down and broad across the back.
  10. Brace softly like you are preparing for contact.
  11. Organize stance first and tempo second.
  12. Start at seventy percent and earn progression.
  13. Build movement from the ground up.
  14. Check bilateral loading before adding speed.
  15. Lengthen the back of your neck.
  16. Choose your base version with intention.
  17. Track knee line before you increase depth.
  18. Feel breath expand the back ribs.
  19. Create space between ears and shoulders.
  20. Anchor core before limbs accelerate.
  21. Set count structure before choreography.
  22. Begin with range you can control.
  23. Align hand, wrist, and elbow before loading.
  24. Confirm foot pressure before turning.
  25. Set your rhythm with one calm exhale.
  26. Commit to clean setup over fast setup.

Breath cues

  1. Inhale to prepare and exhale through effort.
  2. Let your exhale finish before the next count.
  3. Breathe low and wide through your rib cage.
  4. Use a steady warm exhale to reduce tension.
  5. Drop your shoulders each time you exhale.
  6. Match breath length to movement phrase length.
  7. If you hold breath, reduce range and restart.
  8. Inhale to lengthen and exhale to stabilize.
  9. Keep breath moving even inside heavy effort.
  10. Sip air in and pour air out.
  11. Use two longer exhales to downshift quickly.
  12. Let breath pace your effort instead of panic.
  13. Silent inhale, audible controlled exhale.
  14. Breathe into your back body under load.
  15. If dizzy, pause and return to nasal breathing.
  16. Exhale through strain points without collapsing.
  17. Expand side ribs on every inhalation.
  18. Use breath to mark transitions between blocks.
  19. One full breath before you progress layers.
  20. When tempo rises, simplify breath cueing.
  21. Lengthen exhale by one count for regulation.
  22. Keep jaw soft while breath stays active.
  23. Reset with three coherent breaths.
  24. Use breath as your metronome.
  25. Anchor attention on breath quality, not speed.
  26. Finish each phrase with one intentional exhale.

Anatomical Precision cues

  1. Drive from hips rather than lower back extension.
  2. Track knee toward second toe throughout descent.
  3. Press floor away to stand with control.
  4. Keep ribs organized as arms travel overhead.
  5. Rotate through thoracic spine, not lumbar torque.
  6. Hinge by sending hips back first.
  7. Keep heel pressure in lowering phase.
  8. Stabilize pelvis before adding amplitude.
  9. Reach crown and tail in opposite directions.
  10. Let scapula glide instead of pinning rigidly.
  11. Control eccentric phase before chasing speed.
  12. Stack elbow under wrist for loaded pushes.
  13. Use whole foot pressure during transfers.
  14. Move from hip socket not knee collapse.
  15. Create front hip space at end range.
  16. Set shoulder before pressing or pulling.
  17. Maintain neutral neck while output increases.
  18. Use trunk stiffness to transfer force safely.
  19. Keep foot tripod contact during rotation.
  20. Allow rib motion without spinal collapse.
  21. Stabilize first, then mobilize range.
  22. Earn power after precision is established.
  23. Square pelvis when symmetry is required.
  24. Support knee line with glute engagement.
  25. If pinch appears, scale range and realign.
  26. Choose clean mechanics over maximal amplitude.

Effort & Intensity cues

  1. Choose challenge that is hard and sustainable.
  2. Add five percent effort without losing form.
  3. Stay with discomfort, step back from pain.
  4. Let burn inform pacing rather than panic.
  5. You may slow down and still commit.
  6. Strong and smooth can coexist.
  7. Own this repetition completely before progressing.
  8. Push with integrity, not urgency.
  9. Find your edge and breathe there.
  10. Give one more honest set.
  11. Intensity is optional, presence is required.
  12. Scale up only if quality stays intact.
  13. Stay engaged through transition moments.
  14. Effort can be fierce and coordinated.
  15. Keep attention where your body is working.
  16. Sustain before you surge.
  17. Turn strain into structure.
  18. Discipline beats impulse under fatigue.
  19. Half speed can reveal better control.
  20. Anchor and attack with clear mechanics.
  21. Training is challenge without punishment.
  22. Capacity grows with consistent execution.
  23. Finish block with your best movement quality.
  24. Choose steady pressure over dramatic spikes.
  25. Intensity without alignment is wasted effort.
  26. Carry commitment into the final counts.

Emotional & Imagery cues

  1. Move like you are clearing static from signal.
  2. Let each repetition vote for your future self.
  3. Imagine your spine breathing in all directions.
  4. Take space with honesty rather than performance.
  5. Move as if wringing out old tension.
  6. Find the line between grit and grace.
  7. Let breath express what words cannot.
  8. Give shape to what feels unnamed.
  9. Feel your feet as a promise to stay present.
  10. Move from center rather than urgency.
  11. Pour weight into the earth with trust.
  12. Open your ribs like shutters.
  13. Practice courage in manageable doses.
  14. Be strong and soft at once.
  15. Choose expression over perfection.
  16. Let rhythm carry what you no longer grip.
  17. Find dignity inside the work.
  18. Stay curious about sensation details.
  19. Unclench jaw and soften narrative pressure.
  20. Meet yourself without negotiation.
  21. Move like your body can learn today.
  22. Keep one thread of tenderness in intensity.
  23. Let effort become devotional not punishing.
  24. Make room for breath and possibility.
  25. Release looking correct and aim for truth.
  26. Sign this moment with full attention.

Transition cues

  1. Keep breath and change shape on count.
  2. Three, two, one, shift with control.
  3. Pivot to side wall while staying low.
  4. Reset stance before building intensity again.
  5. Carry focus into the next phrase.
  6. Pause, organize, then proceed.
  7. Same rhythm, new direction.
  8. Slow one repetition to regain clarity.
  9. Take one grounding breath before movement change.
  10. Rise from floor in four counts.
  11. Travel two steps and re anchor.
  12. Option to remain at layer one.
  13. Return to center in eight counts.
  14. Shake tension and re enter deliberately.
  15. Hold shape and change tempo only.
  16. Return to baseline then progress.
  17. Orient eyes before next sequence.
  18. Keep pulse while arms change pattern.
  19. Switch lead side on the next count.
  20. If lost, march and rejoin on phrase one.
  21. Breathe first and transition second.
  22. Treat transitions as part of training.
  23. Collect form at the top position.
  24. Use one beat of stillness before go.
  25. Move through handoff with precision.
  26. Clean transitions preserve class coherence.

Closing cues

  1. Let breath arrive before analysis begins.
  2. Notice what changed in this hour.
  3. Acknowledge that you stayed with yourself.
  4. Feel pulse settle under your attention.
  5. Receive the work you just completed.
  6. Thank your body with specificity.
  7. Release shoulders away from ears.
  8. Name one action you did with integrity.
  9. Carry this steadiness into your next task.
  10. Lengthen exhale to signal completion.
  11. Stand in afterglow without rushing away.
  12. Effort counts even when unseen.
  13. One breath for the room, one for yourself.
  14. Soften eyes and widen perception.
  15. Feel feet return to ordinary ground.
  16. Seal practice with one clear intention.
  17. Leave with less noise than you brought.
  18. Integrate before you evaluate.
  19. Make gratitude concrete and specific.
  20. Choose one cue to carry into tomorrow.
  21. Honor limits and growth together.
  22. Read heartbeat as information, not alarm.
  23. Close the loop with a deliberate breath.
  24. Hold center while you transition back to day.
  25. Today was practice in becoming.
  26. Class is complete and integration continues.

Recovery cues

  1. Reduce range and lengthen exhale immediately.
  2. Shift to support position and breathe.
  3. Hydrate your breath before water break.
  4. Scan and release unnecessary tension.
  5. Choose gentler variation without apology.
  6. Let heart rate descend gradually.
  7. Ground feet and orient gaze outward.
  8. Lower intensity to protect tomorrow.
  9. Take two nasal breaths before rejoining.
  10. Recovery is part of performance.
  11. Move softly instead of stopping abruptly.
  12. Shake hands and unclench jaw.
  13. Use longer exhale to downshift arousal.
  14. Return to baseline pattern now.
  15. Respect pain signals and modify fast.
  16. Alternate effort with restoration intelligently.
  17. Recover now to train consistently later.
  18. Give nervous system clear safety cues.
  19. Place hand on ribs and feel depth.
  20. Walk it out with deliberate pacing.
  21. Pause at sixty percent until control returns.
  22. Recovery skill is strength.
  23. Integrate effort rather than collapse.
  24. Back off intensity while keeping technique.
  25. Choose sustainability over heroic spikes.
  26. Finish calmer and more coherent than start.

Practicum

  1. Select eighty cues from this list and map them to your class phases.
  2. Build two cue stacks per phase: one technical stack and one regulation stack.
  3. Test cue stacks in live teaching and annotate response quality.

Deliverable

Create a Personal Cue Deck with at least eighty selected cues, population specific adaptations, and alternatives for trauma sensitive teaching.
